# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    # assigned + labeled — the issues trigger is the dev intake (assignment
    # to the machine login); label events let the pr_approved re-entry and
    # manual agent:review/agent:rework overrides reach the guard. The awf
    # guard skips status-label echoes at evaluation.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read').
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-123');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 3
- **URL**: https://github.com/ajaxspace/dm_tools_app_example/pull/3
- **Title**: gh-2 Create mobile Flutter project with simple login page (Google/Apple sign-in, remember me)
- **Author**: ajaxspace
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-2` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 89
- **Additions**: +3311
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T04:49:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T09:29:23Z

## PR Description

Closes #2
### What changed

Created the mobile Flutter project (Android + iOS) and implemented a login page with email/password sign-in, validation + error states, a **Remember me** toggle that persists the session across restarts, Google sign-in (`google_sign_in` 7.x), and Sign in with Apple (`sign_in_with_apple`, entitlement wired into the Xcode project).

### Key decisions

- Layered auth: `AuthGateway` (provider ops) → `DefaultAuthService` (flows + persistence) → `SessionStore` (`shared_preferences`); `DmToolsApp` restores the session on startup and skips login when present
- Email/password is a local stub (no backend in this example) — swap the body of `DefaultAuthGateway.signInWithEmail` for a real identity API
- Autofill/credential save wired via `AutofillGroup` + `TextInput.finishAutofillContext` (platform password managers); Google credential save rides the plugin; Apple button hidden where Sign in with Apple is unavailable (Apple guidelines)
- Google/Apple plugins resolved to current majors (7.x / 8.x) and wired to their new APIs (`initialize`/`authenticate`, `scopes:`)

### How to verify

```bash
flutter pub get && flutter analyze   # clean
flutter test                          # 35 tests pass (login page widget tests included)
```

Platform builds: `flutter build apk --debug` / `flutter build ios --no-codesign` (needs Xcode for iOS; runtime Google sign-in needs OAuth client config, see README).

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    # assigned + labeled — the issues trigger is the dev intake (assignment
    # to the machine login); label events let the pr_approved re-entry and
    # manual agent:review/agent:rework overrides reach the guard. The awf
    # guard skips status-label echoes at evaluation.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read').
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-123');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 3
- **URL**: https://github.com/ajaxspace/dm_tools_app_example/pull/3
- **Title**: gh-2 Create mobile Flutter project with simple login page (Google/Apple sign-in, remember me)
- **Author**: ajaxspace
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-2` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 89
- **Additions**: +3311
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T04:49:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T09:29:23Z

## PR Description

Closes #2
### What changed

Created the mobile Flutter project (Android + iOS) and implemented a login page with email/password sign-in, validation + error states, a **Remember me** toggle that persists the session across restarts, Google sign-in (`google_sign_in` 7.x), and Sign in with Apple (`sign_in_with_apple`, entitlement wired into the Xcode project).

### Key decisions

- Layered auth: `AuthGateway` (provider ops) → `DefaultAuthService` (flows + persistence) → `SessionStore` (`shared_preferences`); `DmToolsApp` restores the session on startup and skips login when present
- Email/password is a local stub (no backend in this example) — swap the body of `DefaultAuthGateway.signInWithEmail` for a real identity API
- Autofill/credential save wired via `AutofillGroup` + `TextInput.finishAutofillContext` (platform password managers); Google credential save rides the plugin; Apple button hidden where Sign in with Apple is unavailable (Apple guidelines)
- Google/Apple plugins resolved to current majors (7.x / 8.x) and wired to their new APIs (`initialize`/`authenticate`, `scopes:`)

### How to verify

```bash
flutter pub get && flutter analyze   # clean
flutter test                          # 35 tests pass (login page widget tests included)
```

Platform builds: `flutter build apk --debug` / `flutter build ios --no-codesign` (needs Xcode for iOS; runtime Google sign-in needs OAuth client config, see README).

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||

  issues:
    # assigned + labeled — the issues trigger is the dev intake (assignment
    # to the machine login); label events let the pr_approved re-entry and
    # manual agent:review/agent:rework overrides reach the guard. The awf
    # guard skips status-label echoes at evaluation.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice

        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a

  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents

  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read').
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-123');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}

Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 3
- **URL**: https://github.com/ajaxspace/dm_tools_app_example/pull/3
- **Title**: gh-2 Create mobile Flutter project with simple login page (Google/Apple sign-in, remember me)
- **Author**: ajaxspace
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-2` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 89
- **Additions**: +3311
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T04:49:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T09:29:23Z

## PR Description

Closes #2
### What changed

Created the mobile Flutter project (Android + iOS) and implemented a login page with email/password sign-in, validation + error states, a **Remember me** toggle that persists the session across restarts, Google sign-in (`google_sign_in` 7.x), and Sign in with Apple (`sign_in_with_apple`, entitlement wired into the Xcode project).

### Key decisions

- Layered auth: `AuthGateway` (provider ops) → `DefaultAuthService` (flows + persistence) → `SessionStore` (`shared_preferences`); `DmToolsApp` restores the session on startup and skips login when present
- Email/password is a local stub (no backend in this example) — swap the body of `DefaultAuthGateway.signInWithEmail` for a real identity API
- Autofill/credential save wired via `AutofillGroup` + `TextInput.finishAutofillContext` (platform password managers); Google credential save rides the plugin; Apple button hidden where Sign in with Apple is unavailable (Apple guidelines)
- Google/Apple plugins resolved to current majors (7.x / 8.x) and wired to their new APIs (`initialize`/`authenticate`, `scopes:`)

### How to verify

```bash
flutter pub get && flutter analyze   # clean
flutter test                          # 35 tests pass (login page widget tests included)
```

Platform builds: `flutter build apk --debug` / `flutter build ios --no-codesign` (needs Xcode for iOS; runtime Google sign-in needs OAuth client config, see README).

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    # assigned + labeled — the issues trigger is the dev intake (assignment
    # to the machine login); label events let the pr_approved re-entry and
    # manual agent:review/agent:rework overrides reach the guard. The awf
    # guard skips status-label echoes at evaluation.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read').
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-123');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

Interesting: `main()` creates a `DefaultAuthService` and passes it to `DmToolsApp`, but `_DmToolsAppState.initState` creates ANOTHER `DefaultAuthService` and only uses `widget.authService` if non-null. The `authService` param is nullable with a fallback that constructs a new one inside initState — the one created in `main()` is discarded when non-null? No wait: `widget.authService ?? _authService` — in production `main()` passes one, so it's used. But initState still eagerly constructs a second `DefaultAuthService` (cheap, but wasteful and a bit confusing). Minor.

More importantly: security issues to consider.

1. **Email/password stub accepts any well-formed credential** — no real auth. This is disclosed in README/PR ("local stub — swap the body"). It's an example app. Is this a BLOCKING security issue? The PR says it's intentional. It's an example app with no backend. It's disclosed. But there's a subtle issue: `DefaultAuthService.signInWithEmail` validates, and `DefaultAuthGateway.signInWithEmail` validates again — duplication, minor.

2. **SessionStore with shared_preferences** — stores the session (user id, email, name, provider) in plaintext SharedPreferences. Not a token, just identity info. For an example app, fine; could note as suggestion (use secure storage for real tokens).

3. `AuthUser.fromJson`: `json['id']! as String` — if `id` missing, `json['id']` returns null, `null!` throws TypeError. Acceptable for internal persistence, but a corrupted prefs value would crash the app on startup — `restoreSession` is called in `main` via FutureBuilder... Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 3
- **URL**: https://github.com/ajaxspace/dm_tools_app_example/pull/3
- **Title**: gh-2 Create mobile Flutter project with simple login page (Google/Apple sign-in, remember me)
- **Author**: ajaxspace
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-2` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 89
- **Additions**: +3311
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T04:49:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T09:29:23Z

## PR Description

Closes #2
### What changed

Created the mobile Flutter project (Android + iOS) and implemented a login page with email/password sign-in, validation + error states, a **Remember me** toggle that persists the session across restarts, Google sign-in (`google_sign_in` 7.x), and Sign in with Apple (`sign_in_with_apple`, entitlement wired into the Xcode project).

### Key decisions

- Layered auth: `AuthGateway` (provider ops) → `DefaultAuthService` (flows + persistence) → `SessionStore` (`shared_preferences`); `DmToolsApp` restores the session on startup and skips login when present
- Email/password is a local stub (no backend in this example) — swap the body of `DefaultAuthGateway.signInWithEmail` for a real identity API
- Autofill/credential save wired via `AutofillGroup` + `TextInput.finishAutofillContext` (platform password managers); Google credential save rides the plugin; Apple button hidden where Sign in with Apple is unavailable (Apple guidelines)
- Google/Apple plugins resolved to current majors (7.x / 8.x) and wired to their new APIs (`initialize`/`authenticate`, `scopes:`)

### How to verify

```bash
flutter pub get && flutter analyze   # clean
flutter test                          # 35 tests pass (login page widget tests included)
```

Platform builds: `flutter build apk --debug` / `flutter build ios --no-codesign` (needs Xcode for iOS; runtime Google sign-in needs OAuth client config, see README).

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    # assigned + labeled — the issues trigger is the dev intake (assignment
    # to the machine login); label events let the pr_approved re-entry and
    # manual agent:review/agent:rework overrides reach the guard. The awf
    # guard skips status-label echoes at evaluation.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read').
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-123');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 3
- **URL**: https://github.com/ajaxspace/dm_tools_app_example/pull/3
- **Title**: gh-2 Create mobile Flutter project with simple login page (Google/Apple sign-in, remember me)
- **Author**: ajaxspace
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-2` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 89
- **Additions**: +3311
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T04:49:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T09:29:23Z

## PR Description

Closes #2
### What changed

Created the mobile Flutter project (Android + iOS) and implemented a login page with email/password sign-in, validation + error states, a **Remember me** toggle that persists the session across restarts, Google sign-in (`google_sign_in` 7.x), and Sign in with Apple (`sign_in_with_apple`, entitlement wired into the Xcode project).

### Key decisions

- Layered auth: `AuthGateway` (provider ops) → `DefaultAuthService` (flows + persistence) → `SessionStore` (`shared_preferences`); `DmToolsApp` restores the session on startup and skips login when present
- Email/password is a local stub (no backend in this example) — swap the body of `DefaultAuthGateway.signInWithEmail` for a real identity API
- Autofill/credential save wired via `AutofillGroup` + `TextInput.finishAutofillContext` (platform password managers); Google credential save rides the plugin; Apple button hidden where Sign in with Apple is unavailable (Apple guidelines)
- Google/Apple plugins resolved to current majors (7.x / 8.x) and wired to their new APIs (`initialize`/`authenticate`, `scopes:`)

### How to verify

```bash
flutter pub get && flutter analyze   # clean
flutter test                          # 35 tests pass (login page widget tests included)
```

Platform builds: `flutter build apk --debug` / `flutter build ios --no-codesign` (needs Xcode for iOS; runtime Google sign-in needs OAuth client config, see README).

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    # assigned + labeled — the issues trigger is the dev intake (assignment
    # to the machine login); label events let the pr_approved re-entry and
    # manual agent:review/agent:rework overrides reach the guard. The awf
    # guard skips status-label echoes at evaluation.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read').
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-123');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

Interesting: `main()` creates a `DefaultAuthService` and passes it to `DmToolsApp`, but `_DmToolsAppState.initState` creates ANOTHER `DefaultAuthService` and only uses `widget.authService` if non-null. The `authService` param is nullable with a fallback that constructs a new one inside initState — the one created in `main()` is discarded when non-null? No wait: `widget.authService ?? _authService` — in production `main()` passes one, so it's used. But initState still eagerly constructs a second `DefaultAuthService` (cheap, but wasteful and a bit confusing). Minor.

More importantly: security issues to consider.

1. **Email/password stub accepts any well-formed credential** — no real auth. This is disclosed in README/PR ("local stub — swap the body"). It's an example app. Is this a BLOCKING security issue? The PR says it's intentional. It's an example app with no backend. It's disclosed. But there's a subtle issue: `DefaultAuthService.signInWithEmail` validates, and `DefaultAuthGateway.signInWithEmail` validates again — duplication, minor.

2. **SessionStore with shared_preferences** — stores the session (user id, email, name, provider) in plaintext SharedPreferences. Not a token, just identity info. For an example app, fine; could note as suggestion (use secure storage for real tokens).

3. `AuthUser.fromJson`: `json['id']! as String` — if `id` missing, `json['id']` returns null, `null!` throws TypeError. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 3
- **URL**: https://github.com/ajaxspace/dm_tools_app_example/pull/3
- **Title**: gh-2 Create mobile Flutter project with simple login page (Google/Apple sign-in, remember me)
- **Author**: ajaxspace
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-2` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 89
- **Additions**: +3311
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T04:49:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T09:29:23Z

## PR Description

Closes #2
### What changed

Created the mobile Flutter project (Android + iOS) and implemented a login page with email/password sign-in, validation + error states, a **Remember me** toggle that persists the session across restarts, Google sign-in (`google_sign_in` 7.x), and Sign in with Apple (`sign_in_with_apple`, entitlement wired into the Xcode project).

### Key decisions

- Layered auth: `AuthGateway` (provider ops) → `DefaultAuthService` (flows + persistence) → `SessionStore` (`shared_preferences`); `DmToolsApp` restores the session on startup and skips login when present
- Email/password is a local stub (no backend in this example) — swap the body of `DefaultAuthGateway.signInWithEmail` for a real identity API
- Autofill/credential save wired via `AutofillGroup` + `TextInput.finishAutofillContext` (platform password managers); Google credential save rides the plugin; Apple button hidden where Sign in with Apple is unavailable (Apple guidelines)
- Google/Apple plugins resolved to current majors (7.x / 8.x) and wired to their new APIs (`initialize`/`authenticate`, `scopes:`)

### How to verify

```bash
flutter pub get && flutter analyze   # clean
flutter test                          # 35 tests pass (login page widget tests included)
```

Platform builds: `flutter build apk --debug` / `flutter build ios --no-codesign` (needs Xcode for iOS; runtime Google sign-in needs OAuth client config, see README).

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    # assigned + labeled — the issues trigger is the dev intake (assignment
    # to the machine login); label events let the pr_approved re-entry and
    # manual agent:review/agent:rework overrides reach the guard. The awf
    # guard skips status-label echoes at evaluation.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read').
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-123');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

The `authService` param is nullable with a fallback that constructs a new one inside initState — the one created in `main()` is discarded when non-null? 2. **SessionStore with shared_preferences** — stores the session (user id, email, name, provider) in plaintext SharedPreferences. Not a token, just identity info. For an example app, fine; could note as suggestion (use secure storage for real tokens).

3. `AuthUser.fromJson`: `json['id']! as String` — if `id` missing, `json['id']` returns null, `null!` throws TypeError. Acceptable for internal persistence, but a corrupted prefs value would crash the app on startup — `restoreSession` is called in `main` via FutureBuilder... Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 3
- **URL**: https://github.com/ajaxspace/dm_tools_app_example/pull/3
- **Title**: gh-2 Create mobile Flutter project with simple login page (Google/Apple sign-in, remember me)
- **Author**: ajaxspace
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-2` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 89
- **Additions**: +3311
- **Deletions**: -0
- **Created**: 2026-10-20T04:49:01Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-20T09:29:23Z

## PR Description

Closes #2
### What changed

Created the mobile Flutter project (Android + iOS) and implemented a login page with email/password sign-in, validation + error states, a **Remember me** toggle that persists the session across restarts, Google sign-in (`google_sign_in` 7.x), and Sign in with Apple (`sign_in_with_apple`, entitlement wired into the Xcode project).

### Key decisions

- Layered auth: `AuthGateway` (provider ops) → `DefaultAuthService` (flows + persistence) → `SessionStore` (`shared_preferences`); `DmToolsApp` restores the session on startup and skips login when present
- Email/password is a local stub (no backend in this example) — swap the body of `DefaultAuthGateway.signInWithEmail` for a real identity API
- Autofill/credential save wired via `AutofillGroup` + `TextInput.finishAutofillContext` (platform password managers); Google credential save rides the plugin; Apple button hidden where Sign in with Apple is unavailable (Apple guidelines)
- Google/Apple plugins resolved to current majors (7.x / 8.x) and wired to their new APIs (`initialize`/`authenticate`, `scopes:`)

### How to verify

```bash
flutter pub get && flutter analyze   # clean
flutter test                          # 35 tests pass (login page widget tests included)
```

Platform builds: `flutter build apk --debug` / `flutter build ios --no-codesign` (needs Xcode for iOS; runtime Google sign-in needs OAuth client config, see README).

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the factory home (dmtools-agentic-workflows).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agentic-workflows/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (EXPLICIT mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
# required named secret, and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy
# required-secret validation at call time):
#   SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required); AI provider keys ride the generic
#   CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn slots (name via CUSTOM_PROVIDER_KEYn_NAME).
name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'pr_approved' && '✅ pr_approved' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    # assigned + labeled — the issues trigger is the dev intake (assignment
    # to the machine login); label events let the pr_approved re-entry and
    # manual agent:review/agent:rework overrides reach the guard. The awf
    # guard skips status-label echoes at evaluation.
    types: [assigned]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

permissions:
  # The factory (factory-teammate.yml@e611e5f) requests this set and a
  # reusable workflow cannot RAISE rights above its caller — the stub must
  # grant the ceiling or every dispatch startup-fails (live dmtools-agents
  # 2026-10-03: 'requesting actions: write, contents: write, issues: write,
  # pull-requests: write, but is only allowed contents: read').
  actions: write
  contents: write
  issues: write
  pull-requests: write

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-123');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8.
